status_summary: HHS and FDA announced Operation Stork Speed on 2025-03-18; among its six actions it extends the FDA's personal importation policy for infant formula and encourages companies to work with the FDA on clearer labeling, and announces no tariff change, foreign standard recognition or labeling rule. The FDA's program page (updated 2026-07-13) says the personal importation policy first put in place in 2022 continues and does not address recognition of foreign standards. No tariff cut, mutual recognition step or 119th Congress formula tariff bill was found.

timeline.event: HHS and FDA announce Operation Stork Speed, including an extension of the FDA personal importation policy for infant formula and encouragement of labeling transparency; the release announces no tariff change or labeling rule.

title: Liberalize infant formula imports: lower tariffs, loosen labeling, mutual recognition
uncertainties: Whether infant formula faced IEEPA reciprocal tariffs before Executive Order 14389 ended them on 2026-02-20 (see c26-02), and whether the agricultural exemptions in Executive Order 14360 (2025-11-14) cover formula, were not confirmed, because only part of the annex text was read. The personal importation policy is a continuation of a 2022 policy and concerns imports for personal use, so it is a small parallel step; a reader could stage this not_started. Searches performed: four web searches (Operation Stork Speed and imports; a formula tariff bill, which returned only 2022 and 2023 bills; HHS formula actions; mutual recognition of EU formula, which returned only 2022 material) and a Federal Register API query for infant formula (31 documents, titles of the first 20 read, including the 2025-05-14 nutrient request for information and a WIC correcting amendment, none a tariff or recognition action). The nutrient review and WIC bidding are tracked in c10-10.
